title: Arjan and Hargobind
hook: then Guru Arjan and Guru Hargobind

segments.voice: Yesterday: Amar Das and Ram Das, and your line: amar das, ram das. Did you thank someone for quiet service? This week closed Guru Tegh Bahadur's bani and opened the Ardas: the standing prayer, the greeting, Bhagauti, then Nanak, Angad, Amar Das and Ram Das. Today, a father and a son. Day six hundred sixteen.
screen: `AMAR DAS AND RAM DAS — AMAR DAS, RAM DAS.`

segments.voice: In 1606, in Lahore, a man is held by the authorities and dies after being tortured. Sikh tradition remembers him sitting calm through it, saying God's will is sweet. He is the Guru, and his son is eleven years old. What does a boy do with that? This one grew up and did something no Guru had done before: he put on two swords. Then he built a raised platform facing the holiest place in the city. The father had built a house for the scripture. The son built a seat for the community's courage. The Ardas names them in one breath. Today: Arjan and Hargobind.
screen: `LAHORE, 1606.` → `HIS SON IS ELEVEN.` → `TWO SWORDS, AND A RAISED SEAT.`

segments.voice: The Ardas line goes: arjan hargobind no simrau. Remember Arjan and Hargobind. Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru, was the son of Guru Ram Das. He finished the pool at Amritsar and built the Harmandir Sahib in its middle, with doors on all four sides, open to everyone from every direction. In 1604 he compiled the Adi Granth, gathering the hymns of the Gurus before him, his own, and the hymns of saints from other backgrounds, Hindu and Muslim, and installed it in the Harmandir. He wrote the Sukhmani Sahib, the Psalm of Peace, which we read earlier this year. And in 1606 he was executed in Lahore under the emperor Jahangir. Sikhs remember him as the first Sikh martyr. Tradition remembers him living out a line of his own bani, which Sikhs often say as tera bhana meetha laage: Your will is sweet. Guru Hargobind, his son, became Guru as a boy. Tradition says he wore two swords, one called miri, for worldly responsibility, and one called piri, for the spiritual. And he built the Akal Takht, the Throne of the Timeless, facing the Harmandir: a seat of community authority beside the house of prayer. Later he was held in Gwalior fort; Sikhs remember his release, along with fifty-two imprisoned princes, on Bandi Chhor Divas, which falls with Diwali. Put the two together. The father built the house and the book, and gave his life quietly. The son added the sword and the throne, so the community could stand. The Ardas holds both in one breath: the calm and the courage, the scripture and the seat.
screen: `ARJAN: THE HOUSE AND THE BOOK.` · `THE FIRST SIKH MARTYR, 1606.` · `HARGOBIND: MIRI AND PIRI.` · `THE CALM AND THE COURAGE.` · then, large: `ARJAN, HARGOBIND.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: say their names slowly. Sit, settle, breathe. On one out-breath, say: Arjan. Picture a calm face, and four open doors. On the next, say: Hargobind. Picture a young man standing up straight with two swords at his side. Let the names alternate, unhurried. If you pray, you can say tera bhana meetha laage, Your will is sweet, after them. If you don't, think about where you need calm today, and where you need courage. The bell holds the time.
Arjan and Hargobind. The fifth Guru built the house and the book and became the first martyr; his son wore miri and piri, and built the Akal Takht.
Your line: arjan, hargobind. Today, face one thing with calm and one thing with courage, and notice which is which. Day six hundred sixteen.

howItsDone: In every Ardas Sikhs remember Guru Arjan and Guru Hargobind; Guru Arjan's martyrdom is marked each year, often with chhabeels serving cold drinks to passersby, and Bandi Chhor Divas recalls Guru Hargobind's release.

fork.setup: you're eleven, and your father, the Guru, has just been killed in Lahore. tradition says you become Guru. what do you do?
options: put on two swords and build the Akal Takht.
fork.reveal: tradition says Guru Hargobind wore miri and piri and built the Akal Takht facing the Harmandir, so the community could stand.

original.note: Gurmukhi: miri piri, worldly and spiritual authority, the two swords of Guru Hargobind.

trapdoor: what you thought: Arjan and Hargobind are just the fifth and sixth names.
what it means: the book and the martyr, then the sword and the throne: calm and courage in one breath.
what a scholar hears: the Ardas line is arjan hargobind no simrau sri harirai; tera bhana meetha laage comes from Guru Arjan's Asa shabad (Ang 394).

Hargobind's age in 1606 (born 1595, so about eleven): confirm.
Release from Gwalior with 52 princes and the link to Bandi Chhor Divas: traditional; confirm.
